utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, Madam Registrar, would you please call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-12-I, the Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May I have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kenneth Scott for the Prosecutor, I'm joined today by Josee D'Aoust, the assistant in the trial and our case manager, Lakshmie Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Zeljko Olujic, counsel for Mr. Ivica Rajic, and we are meeting today with respect to the scheduling order under the competence of the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will proceed with initial appearance of the accused, Ivica Rajic, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The indictment against the accused was initially confirmed on 29th August, 1995. International arrest warrant was issued against the accused. On the 13th of September, 1996, the indictment was confirmed and again international arrest warrants were issued against the accused. The accused was arrested in Croatia on the 5th April, 2003 and transferred to the detention unit of the International Tribunal on Tuesday, 24th June, 2003. By the order of the president of the International Tribunal, dated 26th June, 2003, this case was assigned to Trial Chamber 1, section A. Mr. Rajic, you have to excuse me for I'm not good at pronouncing your name. I have to ask you several questions. Can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you please give your full name or any nicknames for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My full name is Ivica Rajic and I haven't got a nickname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. What are the date and the place of your birth, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 5th of May, 1958, in the village of Johovac, Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What is the address at which you resided before you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Johovac, Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you family and the embassy of your state informed about your arrest as well as your transfer to the detention unit in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they have been informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Now I would like to ask the Registrar to read out the passage of the Statute of the Tribunal that provides you with the certain number of rights. Madam Registrar, would you please read out Article 20 and 21 of the statute?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Article 20, Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. 1. The Trial Chamber will ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. 2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or arrest warrant of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the International Tribunal. 3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber should then set a date for trial. 4. The hearings should be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Article 21, Rights of the accused. 1. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. 2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to Article 22 of the statute. 3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to the provisions of the present statute. 4. In the determination of any charge against the accused, pursuant to the present statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality: (a) To be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; (b) To have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; (c) To be tried without undue delay; (d) To be tried in his presence and to defends himself in person or through legal assist answer of his own choosing. To be informed if he does not have any legal assistance of this right and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interests of justice so required and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it; (e) To examine or have examined the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; (f) To have the free assistance of the -- of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal. (g) Not to have compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rajic, have you received the indictment against you in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I have received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to read it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you understand its contents or the charges against you in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Have you had any opportunity to discuss the indictment with your counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, would you please read out the indictment, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. The Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Ivica Rajic, also known as Viktor Andric. Indictment, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia pursuant to his authority under Article 18 of the Statute, charges: During October, 1993, the armed forces of the self-proclaimed Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, known as the Croatian Defence Council (HVO), were engaged in an armed conflict with the armed forces of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In October 1993, the town of Vares in central Bosnia was under the control of HVO. Stupni Do, a village located approximately four kilometres southeast of Vares, was inhabited by approximately 250 people who were almost exclusively of Muslim origin. The inhabitants of the village regarded themselves as part of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On or about the 22nd of October, 1993, Ivica Rajic, who was the commander of the Second Operational Group of the HVO based in Kiseljak, came to Vares with HVO soldiers under his command. In the HVO military chain of command, units of the HVO in Vares were under the regional command of the Second Operational Group. On or about the 22nd of October 1993, the HVO forces in or about Vares, including the Bobovac Brigade, came under the direct personal command of Ivica Rajic. On the 23rd of October, 1993, at around 0800 hours or thereabouts, units of the HVO under Ivica Rajic's command attacked the village of Stupni Do. When the attack had been completed by the HVO, at least 16 members of the civilian population had been killed. The village was almost totally destroyed and the inhabitants who had not been killed had been forced to flee.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Ivica Rajic also known as Viktor Andric, son of Ivan, was born on the 5th of May, 1958, in the village of Johovac, in the municipality of Kiseljak, in Bosnia-Herzegovina. He is a graduate of a military academy of the former Yugoslavia and was formerly a captain (first class) in the former Yugoslavia People's Army. In August, 1992, Ivica Rajic became the HVO commander of the Second Operational Group for the region covering the municipalities of Kiseljak, Kresevo and Vares. He occupied this position in October, 1993. General allegations: During October, 1993, a state of armed conflict existed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At all relevant times, the victims and property referred to in this indictment were protected under the applicable provisions of the Geneva Conventions. At all relevant times, the victims and property referred to in this indictment were protected by the law or customs of war. At all times, Ivica Rajic was required to abide by the laws and customs governing the conduct of war and all applicable provisions of the Geneva Convention. Charges: On or about the 23rd of October, 1993, Ivica Rajic as commander of the HVO forces of the Second Operational Group, which included those HVO forces in Vares, ordered an unlawful attack against a civilian population and individual citizens of the village of Stupni Do, causing death and injuries to that civilian population and individual citizens and the almost total destruction of the village. In doing so, Ivica Rajic committed: Count 1: A grave breach of the Geneva Convention of 1949, as recognised by Article 2(a) (wilful killing) and 7(1) of the Statute; Count 2: A grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, as recognised by Article 2(d) (destruction of property) and 7(1) of the Statute; and Count 3: Violations of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3 (deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of the village) and 7(1) of the statute. Or alternatively: On or about the 23rd of October, 1993, Ivica Rajic, as commander of the HVO forces of the Second Operational Group, which included those forces in Vares, knew or had reason to know that a subordinate and subordinates in the HVO was or were about to unlawfully attack and did attack the civilian population and individual citizens of Stupni Do, causing death and injury to that civilian population and individual citizens and the almost total destruction of the village. Ivica Rajic failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such an attack and failed to punish the perpetrators of these unlawful attacks. In doing so, Ivica Rajic committed: Count 4: A grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 as recognised by Article 2(a) (wilful killing) and 7(3) of the statute. Count 5: A grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, as recognised by Article 2(d) (destruction of property) and 7(3) of the statute; and. Count 6: Violations of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3 (deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of the village) and 7(3) of the Statute. Dated 23rd August, 1995. Signed by Prosecutor Richard J. Goldstone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Rajic, you have the right to plead guilty or not guilty to each count, either today or within 30 days from this initial appearance. Shall you fail to enter a plea within this time limit, the Trial Chamber will enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. Are you prepared to enter your plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My suggestion is I will now repeat the individual charges brought against you and I will then ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty to the specific charge. Your answer in each case should be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's begin. Count 1 contains a charge of wilful killing, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Article 2(a) and Article 7(1) of the statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 2 contains a charge of destruction of property, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Article 2(d) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 3 contains a charge of deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of the villages as a violations of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Alternatively, you are charged with count 4 which contains a charge of wilful killing, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Article 2(a) and Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 4, which contains a charge of destruction of property, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 2(a) and Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 6 contains a charge of deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of the village as violations of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 and Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may sit down, please. I'm sorry, there is a mistake because in the transcript I saw two count 4s there, I think the second count 4 should be count 5. May the Registrar please take note that Mr. Rajic has pleaded not guilty to all the counts of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the Registrar will be instructed to fix a date for trial when appropriate. The accused is remanded in custody until further order. He may, however, file a motion on provisional release pursuant to Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. At this stage, are there any matters that the Prosecution wishes to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: May it please the Court, not really this afternoon. We do of course commit to provide the supporting material within the 30 days required by the rule and we anticipate no trouble in doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are there any matters that Defence or the accused wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at this stage, Your Honour. No matters except that we expect the Prosecution within the 30 day time limit to disclose all the supporting material pursuant to the rules so that we can begin the Defence case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any way, I would like to remind the Prosecution that pursuant to Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, it has 30 days to disclose to the Defence in a language which the accused understands all the supporting materials which accompanied the indictment when the confirmation was sought. The Defence is advised that pursuant to Rule 72(A), it will have 30 days period for filing any preliminary motion once it has received all the supporting materials in accordance with Rule 66. For the expeditious preparation of the case, a Status Conference will be scheduled within 120 days from today, pursuant to Rule 65 bis(A). I think that's all for this initial appearance. We will now adjourn the proceedings.
